Preliminary version for the project team. The data come from the 2017 Agricultural Census (IBGE), INCRA/SIPRA (as at 3 June 2025), SEEG 13 (1970–2024) and the 2006 and 2017 Agricultural Censuses. Each value is shown with its reference year. English translation under review. If the two versions differ, the Portuguese text prevails.

Pantanal T5 · Horticultural-irrigated provisional label IBGE code 5106505

Pantanal 80.6% · Cerrado 19.4% of the territory (IBGE, Biomes 1:250,000, 2019). The municipality is grouped by its dominant biome.

RESA Project Manuscript 1 assigns the municipality to type T5, a group of 12 municipalities, in its municipal typology of family farming. The typology applies k-means, with k = 5, to scores from a factor analysis of 21 variables in the 2017 Agricultural Census. Typology details.

Host municipality of the Lambari pilot area. figures being reconciled Project type: Banco da Terra. Pilot-area biome: Pantanal (host municipality’s biome, IBGE 1:250,000, 2019). Field reconnaissance: to be confirmed. Pilot-area page.

The municipality is not the pilot area. The figures on this page describe the whole municipality or all of its family farms. They therefore provide context for the pilot area but do not measure it. Pilot-area figures for families and area will be published only once the sources have been reconciled.

The 2017 Agricultural Census of the Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics (IBGE) recorded 1,684 family farms in Poconé, or 66.0% of the municipality’s agricultural establishments (68.8% for Mato Grosso as a whole). They occupied 49,001 ha, or 5.7% of the area of agricultural establishments, averaging 29.1 ha per establishment (municipal median in the Pantanal biome: 32.7 ha; Mato Grosso mean: 62.9 ha). Persons employed on family farms totalled 4,555. The value of family-farm production was R$17.2 million (2017 values), equivalent to R$10.2 thousand per establishment. Animal production accounted for 61.1% of this value.

In 2017, 5.2% of family farms had a tractor, 3.9% received technical guidance and 6.4% obtained financing (municipal medians in the Pantanal biome: 7.1%, 8.2% and 7.5%). In addition, 86.4% of family farms produced mainly for their own consumption and 11.5% produced cow’s milk.

On land tenure, the 2017 Census recorded 133 family farms in category 46504 (status of grantee or settler awaiting a definitive title), or 7.9% of the municipality’s family farms (10.8% for Mato Grosso as a whole). The Agrarian Reform Projects Information System (SIPRA) of the National Institute for Colonisation and Agrarian Reform (INCRA) records 16 settlement projects based in the municipality, with 881 settled families and 28,243 ha (Report 0227, as at 3 June 2025). Each project is counted only in its host municipality. Category 46504 understates the extent of agrarian reform, because producers who have already obtained their title appear as owners. See Census tenure data and agrarian reform for a discussion.

For 2024, the Greenhouse Gas Emissions and Removals Estimation System (SEEG 13) estimated gross emissions of 1,876.6 thousand tCO2e (GWP-AR5) for the whole municipality, not only for family farming. Of this total, 27.9% came from land-use change and forestry and 66.5% from agriculture and livestock. Removals in the same year totalled 536.3 thousand tCO2e. Between the 2006 and 2017 Agricultural Censuses, the number of agricultural establishments in the municipality (family and non-family farms) rose by 69.1%, and their area rose by 39.9%.
